title: A1 reading check
goal: Show that you can understand short everyday documents (signs, messages, an email, a timetable and an ad) and find the information you need.

example.fr: La pharmacie est ouverte le samedi.
example.en: The pharmacy is open on Saturdays.

example.fr: Le magasin est fermé le dimanche.
example.en: The store is closed on Sundays.
The stop is in front of the bank.

blocks.title: A1 reading: what you can do
blocks.body:
At A1, a reader can understand **familiar names, words and very simple sentences** in everyday documents, and can find **one precise piece of information**: a day, a time, a price, a place, what someone wants.

This check gives you **5 short documents** of the kind you meet in your first weeks in Canada:

- a sign on a door
- a text message from a friend
- a short email from a language school
- a bus timetable
- an apartment ad

**How it works:** read each document, then answer 2 or 3 questions. Every answer is **in the text**: you never need outside knowledge. There are 14 questions. Aim for **80%** (12 of 14) to pass the checkpoint.

**Strategy:** read the question first, then look for the key word in the document. Watch the small words that change everything: [[du… au]], [[et]], [[avant]], [[après]], [[pas de]]. You will not know every word, and that is normal. No dictionary, no translator: this is about what you can do on your own.

steps.title: Part 1: A sign, a message and an email
steps.intro: Read each document carefully, then answer the questions below it.

blocks.title: Document 1: A sign on a pharmacy door
blocks.fr:
PHARMACIE DU PARC
Ouvert du lundi au vendredi : 9 h – 21 h
Samedi : 10 h – 18 h
Fermé le dimanche

blocks.prompt: Can you go to this pharmacy on Sunday?
options: No, it is closed on Sunday.
blocks.explain: [[Fermé le dimanche]] means “closed on Sunday”. The hours 10 h – 18 h are for Saturday ([[samedi]]) only.
optionFeedback: Those are the Saturday hours ([[samedi]]). Look at the last line of the sign.
Those are the hours from Monday to Friday. Look at the last line of the sign.

blocks.prompt: It is Saturday, 7 p.m. Is the pharmacy open?
options: No, on Saturday it closes at 6 p.m.
blocks.explain: On Saturday the hours are [[10 h – 18 h]]. 18 h is 6 p.m., so at 19 h (7 p.m.) it is closed. It closes at 21 h only from Monday to Friday.

blocks.title: Document 2: A text message
blocks.fr:
Salut Amira !
Ce soir, on va au cinéma avec Karim. Le film commence à 19 h 30. Tu veux venir ?
On a rendez-vous devant le cinéma à 19 h.
Réponds avant 17 h, s'il te plaît !
Lucie

blocks.prompt: Why is Lucie writing to Amira?
options: To invite her to the cinema tonight
To tell her the film is cancelled
To ask her for Karim's phone number
blocks.explain: [[Tu veux venir ?]] (Do you want to come?) is an invitation, and [[ce soir]] means tonight.

blocks.prompt: At what time should Amira be in front of the cinema?
blocks.explain: [[On a rendez-vous devant le cinéma à 19 h]]: they meet at 19 h (7 p.m.). The film starts at 19 h 30, and 17 h is the deadline to reply.
optionFeedback: 19 h 30 is when the film starts. They meet before that: [[rendez-vous… à 19 h]].
17 h is the deadline to reply ([[Réponds avant 17 h]]), not the meeting time.

blocks.prompt: What does Lucie ask Amira to do before 5 p.m.?
blocks.explain: [[Réponds avant 17 h]] = reply before 5 p.m. [[Réponds]] is the imperative of [[répondre]] (to answer). Tickets and phone calls are not mentioned.

blocks.title: Document 3: An email from a language school
blocks.fr:
Objet : Votre cours de français

Bonjour Monsieur Nguyen,

Bienvenue au Centre de langues Horizon ! Votre cours de français commence le lundi 8 septembre. Les cours sont le lundi et le mercredi, de 18 h à 20 h, dans la salle 12.

Le premier jour, apportez votre passeport, s'il vous plaît. Le cours est gratuit.

À bientôt !
Sofia Martin, secrétariat

blocks.explain: [[Votre cours… commence le lundi 8 septembre]]. The number 12 is the room ([[la salle 12]]), not the date.

options: On Mondays and Wednesdays, 6 to 8 p.m.
Every day from Monday to Wednesday, 6 to 8 p.m.
On Mondays and Wednesdays, 8 to 10 p.m.
blocks.explain: [[le lundi et le mercredi]] = on Mondays and Wednesdays: two days, not every day from Monday to Wednesday (that would be [[du lundi au mercredi]]). [[de 18 h à 20 h]] = from 6 to 8 p.m.

blocks.prompt: What must Mr. Nguyen bring on the first day?
options: Money to pay for the course
blocks.explain: [[Apportez votre passeport]] = bring your passport. The course is [[gratuit]] (free), so he does not need money.

steps.title: Part 2: A timetable and an ad
steps.intro: Two more documents. Look for numbers, days and small words like [[pas de]] and [[avant]].

blocks.title: Document 4: A timetable at a bus stop
blocks.fr:
Arrêt : Rue Rachel
Ligne 46 — Direction Centre-ville

Du lundi au vendredi : 7 h 15 – 7 h 45 – 8 h 15 – 8 h 45 – 9 h 15
Samedi et dimanche : pas de bus avant 9 h, puis un bus toutes les heures

blocks.prompt: It is Tuesday, 7:30 a.m. When is the next bus?
blocks.explain: Tuesday is in [[du lundi au vendredi]]. After 7:30, the next departure on the list is 7 h 45. The 7 h 15 bus has already left.

blocks.prompt: Can you take this bus at 8 a.m. on Sunday?
options: No, there is no bus before 9 a.m. on weekends.
Yes, there is a bus at 8:15.
Yes, there is a bus every hour all day.
blocks.explain: [[Samedi et dimanche : pas de bus avant 9 h]] = on Saturday and Sunday, no bus before 9 a.m. The 8 h 15 bus runs from Monday to Friday only. After 9 h there is [[un bus toutes les heures]], one bus every hour (like [[toutes les semaines]], every week).
[[Direction Centre-ville]] tells you where the bus is going: downtown. [[Rue Rachel]] is the name of the stop where you are now.

blocks.title: Document 5: An apartment ad
blocks.fr:
À LOUER — Rosemont
Appartement 4 ½ (2 chambres), cuisine et grand salon
Près du métro et d'un parc
1 350 $ par mois
Libre le 1er juillet
Pas d'animaux
Appelez Olivier le soir, après 18 h : 514 555-0172

blocks.prompt: How many bedrooms does the apartment have?
blocks.explain: [[2 chambres]] = 2 bedrooms. In Québec, [[4 ½]] counts all the main rooms (here 2 bedrooms, the kitchen and the living room) plus the bathroom as a “half”.
optionFeedback: [[4 ½]] is the total number of rooms, Québec style. The ad gives the bedrooms in brackets: [[2 chambres]].
[[4 ½]] is the total number of rooms, Québec style, not the bedrooms. Look in the brackets.

blocks.prompt: Amira has a cat. Can she rent this apartment?
blocks.explain: [[Pas d'animaux]] = no animals (no pets). July 1 ([[le 1er juillet]]) is the date the apartment is free, not a rule about animals.
[[Appelez Olivier le soir, après 18 h]] = call Olivier in the evening, after 6 p.m. [[après]] means after; [[avant]] would mean before.

summary:
- Find opening hours, days and times on signs and timetables: [[du lundi au vendredi]], [[fermé le dimanche]], [[pas de bus avant 9 h]]
- Understand what a friend wants in a short message, and what a school asks you to bring
- Read a Québec apartment ad, including [[4 ½]] and [[pas d'animaux]]

meta.notes: All 14 items checked: one defensible answer each, all answerable from the documents. Only change: r10 explanation now glosses toutes les heures.
